section_1.title: The Learning Goal: The 'Game of Guessing'
section_1.content: Introduce neural networks as a black box trying to map inputs to outputs. Define the 'Loss' as the difference between the actual output and the target.
section_1.example: A robot trying to identify a cat; if it guesses 'dog', the difference (Loss) is the distance between the two classifications.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Gradient as a 'Directional Slope'
section_2.content: Visualize the loss function as a mountainous landscape. The goal is to reach the lowest valley (minimum loss). Explain that the 'Gradient' is simply the direction of the steepest ascent.
section_2.example: A hiker standing on a misty mountain slope; they must look at the ground beneath their feet to decide which direction leads 'down' to the village.

section_3.title: The Intuition of Backpropagation
section_3.content: Explain backpropagation as a 'blame assignment' process. We start from the error at the output layer and work backward to adjust the weights layer-by-layer.
section_3.example: A factory assembly line where the final product is defective; the supervisor checks the last station, then the middle, then the start to see which machine was slightly misaligned.

section_4.title: The Chain Rule: The Mathematical Engine
section_4.content: Visually represent the Chain Rule as connected gears. A small turn (adjustment) in the final gear causes a specific, proportional turn in the preceding gears.
section_4.example: A series of interconnected bicycle gears: turning the pedal (input weight) has a multiplier effect on the rotation of the rear wheel (output loss).

section_5.title: Putting It All Together: Gradient Descent
section_5.content: Combine forward propagation (the guess) and backward propagation (the adjustment). Visualize the model iteratively descending the hill until the loss is minimized.
section_5.example: The robot repeats the cat identification task 1,000 times, each time nudging its internal 'gears' based on the error, until it perfectly recognizes the cat.

        # Surface setup
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], z_range=[0, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
